definitions.definition: (countable) An appointment, especially to speak or perform.
(uncountable, by extension, about human emotional state) The feeling of being compelled, drawn in, connected to what is happening, interested in what will happen next.[1]

quote.citation: 2012, James Price Dillard, Lijiang Shen, The SAGE Handbook of Persuasion: Developments in Theory and Practice:
quote.text: In a recent study with a movie recommendation site  […] , higher message interactivity in the form of footprints of user actions, responsive suggestions in a search box, and live-chatting with an online agent led to greater perceived contingency and engagement with the site, which ultimately created more positive attitudes toward it and higher intention to recommend the site to others.

definitions.definition: (countable, uncountable) The period of time when marriage is planned or promised.
(countable, uncountable) In any situation of conflict, an actual instance of active hostilities.
(fencing, countable) The point at which the fencers are close enough to join blades, or to make an effective attack during an encounter.
(uncountable) The quantitative response to a post; attention.
(Internet, countable) A performance metric representing an instance where a user interacts with a post after an impression.
